summary: Wrote pytest regression suite (/app/backend/tests/test_wheelind_backend.py) for Wheelind backend covering auth (admin + OTP), RBAC, driver onboarding (KYC+vehicle), presence prerequisites, fare estimate + min-fare floor, versioned fare configs, full ride lifecycle happy path with financials, state-machine enforcement (start-before-arrived, complete-before-in-progress, arrived-twice, wrong OTP), rider fare increase and status guard, zero-commission subscription earnings, disputes+refund wallet credit, SOS create+list, promotions create+single redeem, and admin dashboard counts. All 22 tests PASS against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Financial arithmetic verified: sedan 5km/15min => 189 total; commission 20% => 37.8, net 151.2, cashback 3.78; zero_commission plan => commission 0 and net==gross.

minor.issue: Non-participant riders/drivers/admins: rider path returns 403 only if user is rider AND not owner; a driver who is not the assigned driver still receives the full ride doc (minus OTP). Consider stricter authorization to hide details from unrelated drivers.

For payment_method='cash' the driver still receives commission_amount as a debit txn on their wallet even though rider did not pay via wallet. Verify intended commission-cash flow; can drive driver wallet negative (allow_negative=True). Not a test failure, but worth documenting.
budget check uses '>' rather than '>=' so a promo can be redeemed exactly to the budget cap; acceptable but worth documenting.

action_items: Consider stricter RBAC on GET /api/rides/{ride_id} for non-participant drivers (currently returns full ride doc minus OTP).
Confirm commission ledger behaviour for cash rides (currently posts debit even if rider paid cash, which can push driver wallet negative).
critical_code_review_comments: Fare/ride math is deterministic and matches published fare formula; good.
presence router enforces KYC-approved AND active-approved vehicle before online; correct.
Fare config versioning: create endpoint properly deactivates prior active version and increments version; verified.
Ride state machine enforced via _driver_and_ride expected_status; verified out-of-order returns 400.
post_transaction consistently updates wallet.balance and inserts transaction with balance_after; ledger integrity looks OK.

dispatch does not exclude drivers whose presence.status is 'on_trip' explicitly, but matching_service filters 'status: online' so on_trip drivers are naturally excluded; watch for regressions if status names change.
generate_trip_otp is exposed to rider via GET /api/rides/{id}; endpoint correctly hides OTP from non-assigned drivers.
compute_earning multiplies by effective_pct only; zero_commission gives net==gross as expected.
test_credentials: Admin admin@wheelind.com/admin123; rider/driver via /api/auth/otp/request+verify (debug_code returned because OTP_DEBUG=true). Tests generate unique phones per run.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_ prefixed users/promotions and a TESTCITY_<run> fare config. No cleanup performed; data persists in wheelind_db (acceptable for shared preview backend).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_wheelind_backend.py and uses pytest-xdist loadscope (configured in /app/backend/pytest.ini). It relies on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env (loaded via python-dotenv). Uses unique run-id-derived phone numbers and vehicle plates to avoid collisions on reruns. Happy-ride and zero-commission flows use dedicated drivers to isolate from other tests; zero-commission uses non-Bangalore coordinates to prevent geographic collision with other online test drivers. If more scenarios are added, keep drivers on distinct coordinates or run offline+online cleanly.
rca of the issue: Initial run had 2 failures: happy_ride and zero_commission fixtures polled offers on the wrong driver because /api/rides/_dispatch matched ANY nearest online driver — parallel tests left multiple online drivers within the 5km radius at the same Bangalore pickup, so offers went to a different driver than the test polled. Fixed by (a) using a dedicated fully-onboarded driver in the happy_ride fixture, (b) placing the zero-commission driver+ride at far-away coordinates so only that driver is a candidate, and (c) polling /driver/offers with short retry backoff to smooth out timing.
